ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60 cm. It is dark brown with thin, white, incomplete crossbands and a distinct white collar. It features a flattened head and enlarged, fang-like anterior maxillary teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lycodon tiwarii* is best distinguished from other Indian wolf snakes by its unique, distinctively broad white nuchal collar that remains unbroken across the nape.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Wolf Snake inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, often found in leaf litter or near human dwellings within low-to-mid altitudinal ranges.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively prowling through forest undergrowth and trees after dark to hunt for small lizards and frogs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon tiwarii* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon tiwarii* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low elevations across the archipelago's tropical forest habitats.
